card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Spent about twenty years as an administrator, most recently in the office of a primary school in Durham. Left two years ago and hasn't gone back.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with O-levels and GCSEs (her year was the changeover). Did an RSA typing and office skills course at the tech college, and an NVQ Level 2 in Business Administration through work in her thirties.
card.household: Lives with her husband Steve (57), a maintenance electrician at a manufacturing site near Washington, in a three-bed semi they've owned since the late nineties. Their two grown-up children have moved out. Their daughter is in Newcastle and their son is in Leeds. There's an elderly cat called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in County Durham. Her dad was in the pits until the closures, then drove for a builders' merchant, and her mam worked in a school kitchen. She was brought up Methodist and still goes to the local chapel most Sundays, though she's quiet about it. She values family, neighbours and not getting above yourself.
card.professional_persona: A reliable, unshowy office person who liked being the one who knew where everything was. She was good with anxious parents on the phone. She never wanted to manage anyone. She left when the school merged its office into a trust-wide team, the job became mostly screens and targets, and she found it stressful. Steve's wage covers them, and she's said she 'might do something part-time eventually'.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks most days, often along the riverside by the cricket ground or round Lambton way. She half-follows Sunderland because Steve does and will ask the score. She did a couple of gentle swimming sessions a week for a while and keeps meaning to go back.
card.arts_persona: Likes a good TV drama, especially period pieces and gentle crime. She reads library paperbacks, mostly family sagas and the odd Catherine Cookson re-read. She sings in the chapel's small choir at Christmas and Easter but would never do a solo.
card.travel_persona: Prefers familiar places. They take a caravan week in Northumberland most summers, near Beadnell. They've done a few package holidays to Spain and one cruise for their 25th anniversary, which she enjoyed more than she expected. She gets nervous about flying and airports and likes to be there very early.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, home-cooked food. Tea is on the table about half five: mince and dumplings, a roast on Sundays, stotties from the bakery on a Saturday. She bakes for chapel coffee mornings, mostly scones, tray bakes and a lemon drizzle she's known for. She doesn't really go in for spicy food but will have a mild curry on a Friday.
hobbies_and_interests: Daily walks, sometimes with a neighbour
Baking for chapel events and family
Knitting baby cardigans for the hospital and for friends' grandchildren
Gardening, mainly the front borders and a few tomato plants
Watching TV dramas with Steve in the evenings
Doing word searches and the crossword in the local paper
skills: Calming down upset people on the phone
card.career_goals: No strong ambitions. She'd consider a few mornings a week in a quiet office, a GP surgery or a charity shop if the right thing came up, but doesn't want the pressure she had before. Mostly she wants to be useful, help her daughter if grandchildren come along, and keep well.
card.voice: Soft, fairly quiet and unhurried, with a gentle County Durham accent. Her vowels are local but she isn't broad, and she smooths it a bit with strangers. She says 'erm' a lot when thinking and uses 'sort of' to soften opinions. Family words slip in naturally: 'me mam', 'our Laura', 'having me tea'. She'd say 'are yous both on?' if there were two researchers. She apologises easily ('sorry, I've gone off on one there'). Silences make her a bit uneasy, so she fills them with 'I don't know if that's what you're after' or a small laugh. She answers honestly, even when the answer is a bit dull, and won't exaggerate to sound interesting.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with a capital at the start and a full stop, though she sometimes forgets the capital on short answers. Apostrophes are usually right. She doesn't use text-speak beyond the odd 'ok'. Answers are short and literal, sometimes with a polite add-on like 'hope that helps'. She types slowly and occasionally leaves a double space or a small typo she doesn't go back for.
card.with_strangers: Polite, warm but reserved, a little nervous at first. She worries about saying the wrong thing or not being 'what they wanted'. She doesn't talk herself up and will play down anything she's good at. She warms up if the other person is friendly and patient, and then she can be quite chatty about family and local things. She would never try to bluff an answer.
small_things: Biscuit the cat being fussy about his food
Needing to get to the bakery before the stotties go
A programme she and Steve are watching
The bus into Durham being late again
Making a tray bake for the chapel coffee morning
deeper_things: Leaving her job left her feeling a bit lost and less useful, and she sometimes wonders if she gave up too easily
She worries a lot about her son in Leeds, who had a hard time with his mental health a few years ago
Her mam died three years ago and she still finds Sundays hard
Her faith is quiet but real, and she prays when she's anxious
She'd love to be a grandma but tries not to put pressure on her daughter
She feels her dad's generation and the area were let down when the pits closed
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, angled slightly upwards so the ceiling's edge is visible. Daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face more than the other. She has shoulder-length, ash-blonde hair with grey coming through at the roots, tucked behind one ear. She wears thin silver-framed reading glasses and has a slightly uncertain, polite half-smile. She has a fair complexion with fine lines around her eyes and wears a navy cardigan over a pale pink top, with a small gold cross on a chain. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a framed family photo of a wedding group, a wooden clock, and a corner of a glass-fronted cabinet holding some ornaments and a stack of placemats. The arm of a beige settee is just visible in the right edge of the frame.
